chapters.3:
As you walk along the creek bed, you notice the sky taking on a grerdish tint with magnetic waves of slata and verado dancing in front of the menagerie of moons and planets in the distance. Truly a fantastic world. Your eyes are then drawn again to the plume of smoke rising from the forest where you had your face bitten off by a plague gremlin. A brief jolt of fear shudders through you at the thought, before you turn back to the mission at hand.

You follow the creek for about a tick, getting slightly distracted again by the unique landscapes and foliage. So far you have only seen small creatures in the wild here, aside from the plague gremlin. You wonder how large the lifeforms get on Talus. The trees don't seem to be exceptionally large but you have only experienced a sliver of this world. This brings forth memories of your last adventure and how you only got to see a small fragment of that world in an entire lifetime.

The creek abruptly ends at a pile of boulders and rubble two lengths high. You think this must be the cave entrance, but couldn't possibly move those boulders. You notice there is a path to keep moving along the rocky wall navigating some thorny branches and a few boulders so you decide to follow this for another entrance into the cave to find the medallion. This path starts to narrow between two walls forming a chasm above you until it ends at a little tunnel that you would have to crawl through. You can see light at the other end but cannot make out anything else besides more rocks.

This may be the alternate route into the caves, so you squeeze yourself through the tunnel, judging it to be a crawl of a few lengths, with only having one mild panic episode where the tunnel narrowed and you were stuck for a mintick. On the other side you see the chasm ends with a group of large abluza crystals jutting out from the rocky wall face. One crystal in the center has a smooth indentation of a perfect circle about a link in circumference. You feel a connection with these crystals and unconsciously approach them and place your hand on the cool indentation. Immediately your being starts to vibrate and tickle until it keeps growing and intensifying, becoming painful. A deafening, unbearable buzz is growing in your head while your bones and insides are quaking until you feel your body literally explode, splattering gore and life plasm over the stone walls and crystals, your scream of agony again echoing in your consciousness as everything goes bleck.

Then suddenly you are screaming, Cecil is screaming, and you find yourself in the cozy farm home of the aged Lizerus. As soon as you get your wits about you, you help Cecil off the floor as your sudden appearance sent them toppling over their chair.

"Wha…? How'd?... But where?..." babbles a bewildered, wide eyed Cecil.

You are echoing their words and confusion in your own mind. What was the comet voice trying to say? How come this reset put you in the middle of Cecil's house? Now that you look around, you see that you are standing in the exact spot you received the abluza Star Sphere. Maybe that connection created a new starting point. Whatever the case, you realize you must tell Cecil the details of your existence, limited as they are, and maybe get some answers yourself.

After explaining the experience of the comet and your first "death", you ask Cecil how long you were gone before popping into their kitchen.

"Fantastic! You were gone for about a tick and trin until you woke me from my nap by screaming in my face. Ha ha, well try not to die anymore, ok?"

So apparently time does not reset when you do; good to know. You are still wondering what actually happens to your avatar when you reset and notice that you are starting to feel a bit fatigued. Not an easy thing on the mind, being exploded, even when it is exploding with love.

You see the wounds on Cecil's leg are getting worse so you get a bowl of water to clean them. Cecil directs you to a cabinet containing some herbs and cloth and how to mix them to make a salve to help with infection. You crush up a twisted yemillow plant called Snarp Root, the dried grerdish brozn leaves of a Mapleweed plant and mix it with some water to make a thick paste that you spread across a thin cloth then wrap it around Cecil's injured leg as they give a deep sigh of relief.

"Ahhh. That's better. Thank you, Lightbringer. Those are common herbs you can find around most wooded areas of Talus, in case you need to heal some other folks on your journey. I guess you don't really need to heal yourself. You can just die and show back up in my house."

You thank them for the knowledge and explain that while you cannot die, you can still feel pain and suffer from infection, so this skill is quite useful. You then offer to go to the well to refill the water barrel and Cecil graciously accepts your help again. You take the remaining bucket to the well, noticing the sky is casting a dull gresh hue as the light from Neb is starting to be eclipsed by some planet slowly shifting across the horizon. You quicken your pace to the well and back as you are not thrilled about seeing what may come out in the darkness of this world.

Once back at the farm, your limbs start to feel extremely heavy and you can barely finish another bowl of charbean soup with Cecil before your eyes start drooping. You survived, sort of, your first rotation on Talus and you lay down upon a thin cloth mat Cecil provided, along with a pillow apparently stuffed with some pleasantly sweet smelling herbs that calm your mind and help your body relax as you drift into a peaceful sleep.

When you wake, the sky is still a gresh hue, but you feel very rejuvenated. Cecil is limping around the kitchen, which is basically where you were sleeping, and they hand you half of what they call a Jeewa Fruit with a pale wheck exterior cracked with yemillow veins and a deeper yemillow interior. Cecil demonstrates by slurping the contents of the middle and then taking a bite out of the rind. You do the same. The yemillow part is so smooth and sweet that it slides easily down your throat. The sweetness is balanced by the bite of the bitter exterior creating a wonderfully unique and exhilarating flavor experience. You realize that you took for granted the myriad of fruits and plants available to you during your first adventure.

While you were sleeping Cecil prepared a small satchel of herbs and another Jeewa for the journey. You wonder what would happen to the bag if your avatar resets but you do notice that your clothes have stayed with you each time, very plain as they are, along with the abluza Star Sphere inside the pocket of those clothes. Something tells you that whatever you want to stay with you, will.

You thank Cecil and travel the route of the creek again, this time at a faster pace, all the while looking out for another possible entrance hidden in the landscape. Nothing stands out to you before you reach the pile of boulders blocking the cave opening. You decide to climb to the top and see if any are loose enough to push off. You strain against a few to no effect, then feel the urge to hold the Star Sphere. Upon close inspection, the inside is like a galaxy swirling in a hypnotic, cosmic rhythm. You feel the power of creation surge through you and are able to easily push enough boulders and rocks out of the way to enter the cave. Even though it did not take much effort, you notice you do feel a bit drained from drawing upon this strange power, and must sit and rest a bit before exploring further.

The cave is extremely dark, but you conveniently find that the Star Sphere is emitting a soft abluza glow allowing you to see a few links ahead. Immediately inside the cave you are met with a decision. To the right appears to be a path that has a gentle slope down, and straight ahead seems to be a long corridor remaining mostly flat with some rock formations extending from the ground and ceiling. You take the path to the right, holding the Star Sphere out in front of you to light the way. This way seems to be gradually spiraling downwards, which you assume is a good thing until the floor starts to crumble into tiny rocks causing you to slip and slide down a suddenly steeper surface that gives way to a bleck abyss. Your Star Sphere casts a warm norangia light upon a field of jagged rocks rushing toward you before you land with a crunch and return to darkness.

A loud "OOF!" escapes you as you again find yourself at the farm. At least this time Cecil wasn't as surprised and you can report to them that you were able to enter the cave. They give you a drink of water before you venture back out to explore the other corridor that surely leads to the medallion. You are getting quite familiar with the path to the cave, as well as a bit frustrated for making so many mistakes thus far. How could a being that is truly mortal survive in this world? It makes you think about the Heroes of the Scorch and how they were able to defeat Starvos, while you meet your demise slipping in the dark. They did have relics of Icosa, so maybe they couldn't die either until they willingly gave up their powers.

Before long you are back at the cave entrance, holding your Star Sphere light out in front to make your way. By taking the corridor straight ahead, you see that you are walking along what must have been the creek bed. It is still dry and dusty and you wonder what has blocked it up if those boulders at the entrance were not the culprit. The path continues on a gradual incline with a few twists and turns. Every now and then you hear the sounds of some creatures in the distance, hoping you do not draw them to you. The air has a very stale smell with it but the further you travel, the more moisture you can feel and you notice a dull yemillowish grerde glow in the tunnel ahead.

You cautiously approach a room that has many glowing strands dangling from the ceiling. They are about as thick as a rope, and have a bulge every link, emitting a yemillow light. On the other side of the room you see another doorway blocked with what looks like frozen water, a hazy abluza sheen. This must be what has happened to the source of the water. You make your way across the room trying not to touch the beautiful plants hanging around you, but that is almost impossible. As soon as one touches you, you feel that it is slimy and sticky. The bulbs of that strand pulse their light and start to wrap around your arm causing you to bump into other strands that latch on and begin to pull you into the ceiling. The more you struggle, the more get activated. Just before you reach the ceiling and feel the strands covering your neck and face, you see the decaying, dehydrated corpse of a large Sapien that you think might be Treywind. Then everything goes dark.

The colors of the world gradually come back into focus, and again you find yourself in Cecil's home with the welcome pleasant smell of charbean soup. The trauma of suffocating by the tentacles of that cave plant along with the horror of the face to face encounter with the remains of another being stuck to the ceiling must be showing on your face as a look of extreme concern projects from Cecil. You describe the experience and they give a soft sob in recognition of your details.

"That does sound like Trey. Thanks to Machiventa, I know they are at peace and have begun their next adventure on a new world. Maybe our personalities will meet again in another galaxy. Let's finish off this soup and see if we can come up with a plan to get past the Glowvine.”

Cecil rummages through a few cabinets and containers searching for tools or tonics that could be used against the Glowvine, but finds nothing. All the farming utensils were almost too rusted to be used for farming and would not stand up to the strong strands of the vines.

"I think you must brave the forest again, Lightbringer. There is a reclusive maverick that stays in those woods. Haven't seen them in quite some time, but their survival skills are advanced and I suspect they have been able to keep the plague gremlins at bay. Perhaps they will be of more use than an old crippled farmer, ha."

You laugh as well, while reminding Cecil that the gift of Machiventa's texts, the Star Sphere, and the soup have been invaluable. In fact, the positivity you feel pulsing in your pocket from the sphere assures you that you will be safe and that you will find what you need to retrieve the Universe Medallion in the forest. Again you thank Cecil for their kindness and inspiration before heading away from the farm and into the woods.

As you reach a clearing that you recognize as the spot of your arrival, you can no longer see smoke rising from the forest. Hopefully you can still find your way to this recluse without encountering plague gremlins or any other fear crazed creatures. Even though the trees and plants of this area have vibrant and lively colors, there is a lingering hint of decay in the air, like death is tightening its grip on the land. You see a few small furry brozn creatures scurry away as you tromp through the forest, along with a group of larger creatures covered in iridescent scales causing reflections of Neb light to dance on the bottoms of the leaves as they slowly graze upon the dying dried grasses on the forest floor.

You are noticing traces of a path winding its way through the trees and you start to follow it, being wary of plague gremlins and strange plants that may eat you. Soon you see the outline of a cabin forming in the distance so you increase your pace, eager to meet another being aside from Cecil. You stop about 5 lengths away and you can see that this cabin is sturdy and well maintained with thick dark brozn logs interlocking perfectly topped by a peaked roof made from thinner branches and leaves. A large stone fire ring is off to the side, along with a heavy wooden table stained with what looks to be blood.

While studying the cabin, you take a few steps then feel a twig snap under your foot. The world turns upside down as your leg is yanked upward by some thick vine rigged to a tree, leaving you hanging and spinning trying to free your foot. Not only did this disorient and trap you, it caused other branches to bang against a hollow log creating a cacophony of clanks and clunks to echo throughout the forest. While struggling with the vine you see the door to the cabin open and a large four legged beast with gresh and bleck fur races toward you emitting sharp shrill noises and flashing a mouth full of pointed teeth. Behind that, an even larger Sapien covered in light rojed and light yemillow fur emerges and rushes after the beast. Still spinning and now panicking, the beast closes in every time you blink. Once it reaches a length from you, you see madness in its eyes and froth in its mouth as it uses its powerful legs to launch itself toward you.

You brace for the impact but instead feel a rush of wind and the thunk of the collision behind you as the beast slams into a plague gremlin that was about to dispatch you. The beast makes quick work of the gremlin by latching its jaws around the neck and shaking vigorously. The gremlin's claws dig into the beast but come away with only clumps of fur before it goes limp and drops to the ground emitting a foul smell of decay. Suddenly the Sapien is upon you brandishing a shiny bleck stone knife and swiftly slices the vine, dropping you onto your head. They grab you with one arm, easily sling you over their shoulder, and head back into the cabin.

Once inside, you are thrown to the ground and the beast pins you to the floor.

"What are you doing around here? You know how long it takes to set that trap up? AAARGH! Almost got a live gremlin. YOU almost ended up a smear on the forest floor if it weren't for me and Wooly there," the Sapien rants in a deep gravelly voice while pacing and waving their arms inside the cabin.

All the while, Wooly's head is hovering over yours with intense brozn eyes and huffing hot, foul smelling breaths into your face. You are not entirely sure what has just happened, as all these events spanned less than a mintick. You stammer a bit, unsure of how to answer and then a drop of Wooly's saliva falls into your throat causing you to cough and heave. The Sapien makes a click sound that makes the creature jump off your chest and lay in a corner, still staring at you intently. You are hauled up to your feet and given a few thudding slaps on the back causing you to cough more.

"Alright, get it all out. Seriously though, what are you doing in my woods? Good way to get yourself killed by those cursed gremlins."

You clear your throat and pull some Wooly fur from your mouth before introducing yourself. You are completely honest, reciting your whole experience with the comet, Cecil, the Star Sphere, and your many deaths so far.

"Well that's quite the story. You're lucky not to have added another death to your tally. I'm Brontu, and you've already got too acquainted with Wooly there. Seems that you owe me one of them lives of yours, and I got just the use for it. I was jumped by a gang of those jerkin gremlins while hunting, and dropped my stringbow and arrows. You go and get it while I reset my trap you destroyed."

Brontu then tells you how to get to the area where they lost their stringbow, being careful to detail the many spots along the way where they have set traps and how to avoid the debacle that introduced you. With that, Brontu proceeds to stomp around the cabin grabbing different pieces of equipment and muttering to themselves. During this whole exchange, Wooly has been staring at you, unblinking, so you decide to slowly back out the door and head in the direction Brontu indicated. You notice a few of the traps they mentioned and are able to avoid them as you continue on this worn hunting path traversing through thin yemillow barked trees and tall dying grasses until the landscape changes to an open, rocky terrain with the crumbled remains of long abandoned stone walls and buildings.

Behind one of the walls you see the stringbow and arrows, but also see three plague gremlins a couple lengths away. They seem to be distracted by mutilating the corpse of some poor creature. You manage to sneak over and silently grab the gear without being noticed. As soon as you sling the arrow bag over your shoulder, the munching stops and you see all three gremlins staring at you. When they start running toward you, you think about using the stringbow on them, but instead you feel a tug from the abluza Star Sphere in your pocket. Instinctively you grab it and feel a deep hum in your throat. Your mouth opens and the hum expands; the harmonic frequency almost lifts you off the ground and fills you with love.

The gremlins immediately stop, stand on their hind legs, and sway looking straight up while matching the hum emitting from you. Their hard bleck and rojed exterior starts to melt away into a pale abluza color until abruptly the humming stops. You fall to your knees laughing uncontrollably in joy from the vibration of love still echoing through you. The transformed gremlins scurry away chirping and playing, obviously experiencing the same joy as you. As you get back to your feet, your vision starts to dim and you feel a bit light headed almost causing you to return to a knee. A smile is still stuck on your face, but the use of the Star Sphere has physically drained you causing all your muscles to ache.

You wonder how you were able to create that noise and why it affected the gremlins in such a way. When you think about it, an answer forms in your mind. Love. Fear melts in the presence of true Love. You vibrated with the frequency of the Love of the universe and destroyed the Fear infecting those creatures. What an amazing sensation. You continue to feel the buzz all the way back to Brontu’s, noticing all the colors of the world vibrating on a higher level with you, and you seem to fly back to the cabin despite the exhaustion felt in your body.

You come upon Brontu and Wooly covering up their recently rigged snare trap with some of the surrounding dry brush. The vibration still emitting from you, seems to wash over them as you approach and see their features soften. Wooly starts shaking their backside and doing little hops with their front legs. A laugh and a smile come from Brontu when they see Wooly’s dance and notice you with their stringbow and arrows. The explanation of the encounter with the gremlins spills out of you with your mind and mouth still racing from the experience.

“Ha, you actually did it! I was half expecting to find you dangling from another one of my traps. The other half was expecting you to be a blood stain on the ground. You say those jerkin gremlins transformed? And ran away? There does seem to be some energy about you that I can’t quite figure out.”

Wooly gives a shrill emote in agreement and Brontu pulls their shiny bleck stone knife from their belt, handing you the hilt made of wood and wrapped in the soft hide of some creature.

“Here, it’s the least I can do for getting my gear back. This should be able to take care of that Glowvine in the cave, no problem. Hopefully you can clear out these gremlins and bring the water back. Luck be with you on the rest of your journey.”

Brontu and Wooly stride back into their cabin, leaving you standing with a silly smile stuck on your face, knife in hand, gazing into the sky now colored a dark rojed hue. Your body is still aching from activating the Star Sphere, but you feel like you have taken too much time and made too many mistakes to take a rest, so you make your way back to the caves eating the Jeewa fruit from your pack to regain some stamina. It tastes even more wonderful in your euphoric state. Maybe this vibration of Love enhances everything.

The terrain is becoming much more familiar and less distracting, letting you reach the cave in just under a tick. You hold the Star Sphere in front of you, grateful for its soft abluza light in the dark tunnels. You carefully make your way until you see the yemillowish glow indicating the entrance to the Glowvine room. Star Sphere in one hand, knife in the other, you hack at the reaching, pulsing tentacles; glancing up at the ceiling to see the constricted body of Treywind along with another corpse that you recognize as your own, answering your question about what happens to the avatar when you die. Yet you still wonder how the Star Sphere stayed with you. If you were to pull down your body, would there be another Star Sphere in their pocket? The thought of trying repulses you and you have made it to the archway of the next room, leaving a trail of severed, lightless vines in your wake.

The way is blocked by what looks like murky water filling the whole room. Upon touching the abluza brozn surface, it is harder than it looks and has a warm feel to it. You feel a tug from the Star Sphere and decide to try the hum that worked on the gremlins. You are able to recreate the sensation, but something feels off and the wall remains solid. Another stronger tug from the Star Sphere causes you to touch it to the mysterious wall sending a harmonic flash into your mind and a higher pitched frequency to burst from your mouth.

The wall starts to shimmer and wave with the frequency allowing your hand and the rest of you to move forward into this murky solid material. The substance is resistant and is like moving against a strong current or wind, but you maintain your vibration to slowly push your way through. Unsure of where to go, you rely on the Star Sphere to guide you, but after a few minticks your muscles start to ache and you are not sure how much longer you can hold the vibration. You try not to think of what might happen if this room became solid with you in the middle. A renewed sense of determination fills you as you get a glimpse of a slata object a couple lengths away.

You push the frequency harder, your muscles are bulging and straining, your voice begins cracking, your vision is starting to fade, but you are getting closer. You stretch the Star Sphere in front of you toward what you now know to be the Universe Medallion. Bleckness fills your eyes, but you keep pushing forward. Your muscles are screaming, but you are almost there. Your voice starts to crack and falter, causing the pressure of the room to increase making you unable to breathe. As the bleckness and pressure embrace you, you give one more desperate gasp and lunge, barely touching the abluza Star Sphere to the medallion.

This contact causes an explosion of light and rushing water. The Universe Medallion slams into your chest, melting into your skin with a sensation of ecstasy and anguish. A torrent of water is flowing around you, but you stand solid and unmoving as it empties out of the cave and into the creek. The pure wheck light enveloping you gets stronger and you start to feel your avatar dissolve, but your consciousness remains, growing stronger as you float away from the cave, away from Talus, past the comet that brought you here, past the galaxies and constellations until you seem to be sitting at a universe in the center of all universes. You are inside of time. The silence penetrates every part of your being and every being you are a part of. A light of pure love fills your soul and delivers a message.

“Lightbringer, know this. The universes were created from unconditional Love. There is a great and glorious purpose in the march of these universes through space. All of your mortal struggling is not in vain. We are all part of an immense plan, a gigantic enterprise, and it is the vastness of the undertaking that renders it impossible to see very much of it at any one time and during any one life.”

“We are all a part of an eternal project which the Creators are supervising and outworking. There is in the mind of the Creator a plan which embraces every creature of all the vast domains, and this plan is an eternal purpose of boundless opportunity, unlimited progress, and endless life. And the infinite treasures of such a matchless career are yours for the striving! Go now, Lightbringer, carry the Love of the universe with you to shine your Light upon Fear.”

The truth and hope of this message resonate with every molecule of your being and as the light fades, you begin to fall. The universes and galaxies rush past you again as you travel back to Talus, but instead of going to the moon, you slam into the comet that brought you here. Space, time, and sound all come rushing back to you at once when you find yourself in the cool stone room you arrived in. This flood of emotions and sensations overwhelm you and you collapse on the floor as everything goes dark.
chapters.4:
"Is it alive?"

"I don't know, go poke it."

"You poke it, I was the one that cleaned up the mess it made on the floor."

You give a soft moan as you feel some tapping on your head. The world is still spinning as you clutch your chest where the medallion struck you and can trace the thick circular outline of it slightly protruding from underneath your skin. There are a couple of creatures in the room with you whose features light up at your movement. One is a small being excitedly bouncing up and down clapping their hands. They have smooth brozn skin, dark eyes, and puffy, curly, bleck fur growing out the top of their head. The other is a taller creature with pale verado skin, deep anildigo eyes and wheck boney horns that curl back from the top of their head.

"Greetings, Lightbringer! I am Bruxanna Barr, founder of the Icosa Castle Comet welcoming committee, so, welcome. We are so super excited you have chosen to help us with the Fear Rift. How do you feel? You died a lot. Did it hurt? Ooh, can I touch the medallion?" Says the Melkin that you recognize as the voice that you first heard when you arrived.

The Dimoneesh addresses you with a more controlled tone.

"It is indeed a pleasure to have you here. I am Wexler Krosh Creadus, a Perfector of Wisdom for Project Lightbringer. We were able to see the broadcast of your experience once you obtained the Supernal Star Sphere of Sound. Bruxanna is correct, you perished many times. I was concerned you were going to deplete our surplus of Life Plasm. Now that you have the Universe Medallion, we can proceed with the next missions. There are…"

"We have plenty of time for that later, Wex. Let's show them around the castle, get settled in their room; you saw how difficult it was for them," interrupts Bruxanna.

"It's Wexler, and…"

"Uhgghh! Ok, WEX-LER! You can drone on about the missions while I give the grand tour. Come on, Lightbringer," Bruxanna says as they grab your hand to lead you through a stone archway, leaving Wexler standing there rubbing their brow just below their right horn.

You enter a large simple common room that Bruxanna calls the barracks. It has a long wooden table and chairs and connects to many rooms identical to the bland room you just came from. The dull monotone of the castle is quite underwhelming after the colors of Talus, but you entertain the Melkin's excitement. They lead you through a corridor out into an expansive courtyard with a fantastic view of the Nebrom system overhead and a circle of abluza crystals in the center protruding from the pale gresh rocky surface of the comet.

“This is the Teleportation Station where we are able to attune to sacred locations and objects on Talus. Wexler is still learning how it works…”

“I know how it works,” interrupts Wexler. sharply “I just need to calibrate it with the Lightbringer and the Universe Medallion whenever you are done with the tour. No rush. Not like worlds and galaxies hang in the balance.”

Bruxanna leans close and whispers, “Wex has been going crazy trying to figure that thing out. It almost exploded when you found the medallion.”

Now switching to a louder tone, Bruxanna says “Alright, let’s get you to your room so you can relax and process all of this. Luckily your room is right over here connected to this courtyard and the Teleportation Station. I’m so excited to see this.”

You are led to a room with thick, wooden, double doors and simple smooth metal handles. Bruxanna motions for you to open the door, practically giggling in anticipation. As you grab the handles, the medallion embedded in your chest starts to tingle and you can feel it tickling your mind and memories. The doors open and it is a simplified version of what you had in your mind as the perfect room. Bruxanna lets out a loud whoop and laugh before running past you and jumping onto the bed with a flop.

“Wow, this room was totally empty and dull before you opened it. I know, I checked right before you got here. I’m so jealous. Can you make my room like this?”

“EH-HEM!” Wexler coughs loudly at Bruxanna. “I think we can let them have some quiet so they can relax and change as you suggested. Lightbringer, we will be awaiting you at the Teleportation Station, at your leisure.”

With that, Wexler drags Bruxanna out of your room and gently closes the doors. Now that you are alone again, your exhaustion overpowers you and you also flop onto the bed. While your body rests, your consciousness travels away from the avatar, connected to the All Spirit. You immediately arrive at the central universe, immersed in the light of the Creator and you can feel your energy recharging. This time there are no words or thoughts appearing in your mind, just Love. The time you spend here feels like an eternity, but also like an instant before you are rushed back to your room in the castle Comet.

You awaken, buzzing with energy from the Love of the Creator. Looking around your room, you see many things from your previous life that stir pleasant memories for you. There is an area of the room with a variety of clothes hanging and you realize you are still wearing the bland, shabby, and now filthy clothes you appeared with on Talus. You also notice an unpleasant odor emitting from you and wonder if there is a place to clean yourself. There does not seem to be any water anywhere, but there is a small room that contains a shelf with a series of five brozn jars and a bucket in the corner.

All of the jars contain a faintly scented foggy ointment, but only one of them smells pleasant to you. Instinctively you know this to be a salve for the body of your avatar so you discard your ragged clothes and apply the soothing lotion to your body, again finding it a strange sensation to trace the Universe Medallion's slight bulge from underneath your skin just below your throat. It doesn't hurt, quite the opposite actually; a steady stream of joy seems to be coursing through your being. Your body drinks up the ointment leaving you feeling clean and refreshed.

You go over to the hanging clothes and pick out an outfit that feels practical yet stylish, making sure you still have the pack that Cecil gave you containing the herbs. Everything fits perfectly and you are eager to learn more about this place along with the next missions. As you open your door to enter the Teleportation Station, Bruxanna falls to your feet giving a little squeal.

"EEK! OOF! Lightbringer! I… Uh, ha ha…" the Melkin stammers.

"We were just bringing you some nutrient paste to ease your hunger after your rest," interjected Wexler carrying a platter of exactly what you imagined nutrient paste to look like.

Bruxanna makes a gagging sound,

"It's best to just swallow it in one go so you don't have to taste it," they say as they scoop some up with their fingers and shove it into their mouth, giving an audible swallow.

Wexler gives a bit of a sneer in disgust, "It has all the components necessary to maintain our life plasms and we have extremely limited resources at our disposal. I will concur the taste leaves something to be desired, but nonetheless…"

They hand you a small dish of the paste along with a thin, yet wide stick. Wexler demonstrates by collecting some nutrient on the stick and transferring it to their mouth. You do the same and find that it has no real taste to it at all, while having a bit of grittiness. Oh how you wish you had a Jeewa fruit with you to share with them. You describe the flavor sensation of the fruit from Talus and see Bruxanna drooling as they wipe paste from their hand onto a small soiled cloth hanging from their belt. You ask the pair how they came to be here, how many others are in the castle, and what it is they actually do.

"Bruxanna and I are ascending mortals from different evolutionary paths; we volunteered to be one of the twenty custodians for Project Lightbringer as our next spiritual journey, but sadly, due to an inconceivable routing and programming error, only a few of us made the voyage launch," Wexler says giving a harsh glance toward Bruxanna.

"I thought the crystal launching station was a musical instrument and off we went. It was bad and we had been trying to maintain this castle ourselves for many rotations as we made our way to Talus. We didn't even get to eat at the banquet for the orientation," Bruxanna admitted quietly.

"The point is, we are severely understaffed, undersupplied, and unprepared for this project, but, under my guidance, we can make this the most successful Fear Rift closure in Dalamatia history," states Wexler confidently. "Let's get to the Teleportation Station where we can map out our next mission."

You ask about the Fear Rift to hopefully get a better idea of what your role is in all of this. Wexler explains that a Fear Rift occurs when a world's Celestial City gets destroyed, or the Planetary Protector rebels against the Love of the Universe. These are rare occurrences, but can seriously derail the spiritual evolution of the mortals of those worlds. Fear Rifts, if unchecked, can spread to other worlds and galaxies like an infection. From what they understand about Talus, Starvos was a manifestation of Fear expanding from another galaxy that destroyed the Celestial City or severely damaged it so that it cannot give or receive broadcasts. Wexler says our mission is not just to find and seal the Fear Rift, but to learn the whereabouts and condition of Lanaforge, the Planetary Protector, as well as the Celestial City of Turantia itself.

"We have no idea how to close the Fear Rift and were hoping you had some insights into that part of the operation, but you seem to have no knowledge at all," Wexler says plainly. "It may be important to locate Machiventa Melchizedek on Talus as we are in great need of their wisdom."

Wexler steps into a semicircle with a variety of abluza crystals. The Dimoneesh begins to hum as they touch specific crystals and a map appears in the air in front of them with different areas flashing and focusing with various colors. Nothing looks familiar to you but Bruxanna points to a spot and tells you that is the place they first placed you. Wexler stops humming and explains what they think the different colors mean.

"From what I can discern, the dull abluza color represents an artifact of Icosa, and the other hues of the spectrum are the remaining Supernal Star Spheres. This area covered in bleck and gresh, I believe, is the remnants of Turantia."

There is a section near the top right of the map with a yemillow glow but under that glow is a faint flashing wheck light. You reach over Wexler to point out the flash and inadvertently grab onto one of the crystals. The Universe Medallion immediately ignites in your chest causing you to emit a high pitched harmonic tone as bright light blinds your vision. You feel a great pressure and a disruption to your equilibrium as light and sound come flooding back to your senses. There is a roar of voices, an odor of overheated creatures, and a sight of many large grerde lifeforms covered in bulbous warts, surrounding you while wielding wooden sticks and clubs. Two of these creatures grab and bind your arms, two bind your legs, and one slams a club to your head causing everything to go dark.
chapters.5:
You awaken stiff and aching all over, unable to move much of your body. You can feel you are sitting upright, tied to a tree or post with thick vines around your chest and thinner vines binding your feet together. Once the ringing in your head clears, it is replaced by raucous chanting from the wart covered beings that captured you.

"CRON-GROT!"

"CRON-GROT!"

They keep chanting this as they bash their clubs and stick together. You begin to panic and feel Fear start to creep into your mind until the wave of Love and joy from the medallion washes over you. You call upon this energy to free yourself and a soft abluza light emits from your throat as the harmonic frequency vibrates the vines binding you, but it does not seem to loosen them.

"HA HA HA, stop, HA, stop it, hee hee," a voice startles you from your left side as you see a Melkin bound next to you, wiggling and giggling with the vibrations of energy coming from you.

"Hoo hoo! What? The? Luck? Icosa, you are crazy, ha ha! I know that frequency, friend. Ha! Let's get outta here," the Melkin exclaims as they then start to make gagging and choking sounds.

You look to see what is happening to them and they appear to be trying to regurgitate something, all the while, the grerde beings are doing their chant, seemingly oblivious to the actions of the captured. For the first time you really observe your surroundings to see a soggy, mossy terrain thick with the smell of mold and fungus. The trees appear to be mostly dead, colored bleck with dark grerde interspersed with many felled and rotting in the mucky ground. To your right you see a tall cave opening on the side of a hill about ten lengths away which appears to be where all of the chanting beings are focused. You also see a few other beings tied up to trees like yourself and the heaving Melkin who manages to vomit something up and catch it in their hand.

In this same moment you see a creature emerge from the cave moving in jerking, erratic steps causing your captors to erupt in cheers. The creature, you assume is Cron Grot, looks to be the same lifeform as the wart covered beings except it seems to be fused with metal on various parts of the body, most notably one appendage extending from the shoulder fashioned into a flexible spike. The metal appears to be hammered and melted directly into the skin. The heavy creature shuffles toward the first group of captives, picking up speed as the chanting rises. There is a mindlessness to this creature, as if being controlled by other forces.

You watch in horror as Cron Grot gently presses the spike in the face of a screaming captive. The screaming is replaced by a grotesque sound of suction as a bleck aura flows from the face into Cron Grot. This process takes only half a mintick before leaving a shriveled husk where once was a living being.

"Here, take this," the Melkin says with bile and saliva dripping from their mouth while struggling to put it in your hand around the bindings. Before you can object, the yemillow Star Sphere touches your hand, immediately vibrates through your skin and travels to the Universe Medallion in your chest. You feel it click into place and a surge of Love electrifies all of your muscle fibers, hardening and expanding them. A yemillow aura forms around you and with a slight flex of your growing muscular appendages, the vines snap, freeing you and the Melkin.

Your legs pulse with strength as you leap over to Cron Grot just before it is about to press the spike into another captive. They have an emptiness in their eyes and don't even register your presence as you grab their spike hand and curl it up on itself, rendering it useless. In the same motion, you place your hand on Cron Grot's face and activate the Star Sphere of Sound causing abluza light along with a warm hum to expand from your mouth and hand. The monstrosity immediately goes limp and the bleck aura dissipates into the wind as a heavy silence falls over the crowd.

The rush of energy you received fades fast as your auras dissipate as well, and you collapse to a knee next to Cron Grot. The Melkin has surprisingly quickly untied all of the captives and directs them to the cave while the stunned captors stand staring blankly, still not understanding what is going on. Finally a roar rings out causing them all to surge toward you waving their clubs. As you get to your feet to join the others, the Melkin sprints past you toward the mob.

"That was super! Get to the cave, I'll be right back," they say before doing a little hop and sliding in the mud under the legs of the advancing wart creatures. You pick up your pace but keep looking over your shoulder for a sign of your fellow captive. As soon as you reach the cave opening, you hear a faint harmonic chord followed by a pop and see the Melkin soar through the air over the top of the horde, landing a length in front of you holding a twisted wooden staff that has an open circle at the head with strands of thin vine stretched across it. The impact causes an unnatural wave of mud to launch behind them, washing away the pursuers but also sealing the cave opening with debris just after you and the Melkin roll in to join the other captives.

As the dust settles, the dull glow from your medallion illuminates the terrified beings huddled together. The flying Melkin brushes the mud from their already ragged clothing and addresses everyone.

"Well then. That was awful. I am Machy Mel and I'm terribly sorry we had to meet this way. Let's rest here to regain our energy," Machy says as they pluck on the strings of their staff, activating a bright and warm norangia light at the tip.

There are two Leyf lifeforms, along with a Sapien that made it into the cave. They immediately slump down against the cave wall, exhausted yet relieved. Machy strums another chord and you see a faint rojed sheen stretch across the collapsed cave opening. Could this be the Machiventa that sent the knowledge orb about the history of Talus, and that gave Cecil the Star Sphere? They did give you the Sphere that triggered the strength to escape, but they look so young. The Melkin has no visible hair, deep bleck skin, and bright abluza eyes. They are wearing what looks like a rough brozn sack secured around their waist with a worn woven cord, but it is hard to tell in the dim light and the mud. Machy inspects the rojed barrier and gives a nod before walking over to you.

"Hoo-wee! That was some show, Lightbringer. I see you found the Supernal Star Sphere of Sound. How are Trey and Cecil? Fun times with them," they say, trailing off whimsically.

You sadly explain how Treywind perished looking for the Universe Medallion, and that Cecil has been injured by plague gremlins.

"Ouch! Those plague gremlins. Me and you, Lightbringer, we're gonna purify the world of those things. Once we can figure out their source. I am saddened yet excited for Trey! They were so thirsty for the knowledge of the afterlife, and now that adventure has begun. So what's it like being you? How did you get here? I have been waiting FOR-EV-ER! I do have to say the timing was perfect. That's going in my next broadcast, for sure. Epic!"

You tell the story of your arrival on Talus and all the hardships endured. Machy’s abluza eyes eagerly absorb your information, and you notice the other captives have perked up to listen.

“Wow! I believe it, Lightbringer. You have come to this world at a rough time, but, that is kind of the point of your existence. Hope you are ready.” Machy flashes a smile and pats your arm, adding, “Let's go over our next steps and then get some rest before we move through this cave.”

For the first time since you accidentally teleported to Talus, you think about Bruxanna and Wexler and how confused they must be at your vanishing. Suddenly you hear voices from behind you.

"Try humming a different frequency."

"I've been trying. Don't touch that, you are going to make it worse."

"How could I make it worse? You lost the Lightbringer."

You spin around and only see the dark cave wall, but you recognize the voices as your companions from the Castle Comet. To the concern of the beings in the cave, you call out to the voices in your head.

"Oh thank Icosa," you hear Wexler say with a huge sigh. "Where have you gone? This is certainly not part of the protocol, but it appears that our connection is stable now and we are getting a clear broadcast from you now though the image is quite dark."

You briefly outline your recent encounter and hear Bruxanna shriek at the mention of Machiventa. You ask them if they know what happened and if there is a way to get back, but are only met with a bit of stuttering and stammering from Wexler until Bruxanna interjects.

"No clue, but we will keep working on it from our end. You found Machiventa without even trying, so just keep following the Love, Lightbringer. Castle Comet out," and you feel your mental connection with them end, leaving you looking at the confused beings in the cave after they witnessed your one sided conversation.

"Who ya talkin to there, champ?" Machy says breaking the silence. "You know what, not important, always thought the Lightbringer might be a little loopy.

Machy Mel explains the beings that captured you are the Lerp lifeforms, a primitive cousin of the Leyf beings. Machy was investigating the Fear corruption infecting the Lerp in this area. After the emergence of Cron Grot, they think this cave will hold some clues to the origin of that monstrosity and the location of the Fear Rift. The excitement has worn off and the exertion of using your medallion powers has left you exhausted. As you lay down on the damp cave floor, Machy dims the light from their staff and begins plucking a soft melody that carries you gently to sleep.

Unfortunately your sleep is full of terrible, jumbled visions. Scenes of lava surging violently in the center of a charred obsidian structure fashioned with jagged spikes at every corner and joint. Masses of horrifically disfigured, metal fused slaves, digging and building obsidian structures. You zoom through a dizzying labyrinth of dark tunnels, all the while a shrill sound of metal pounding metal creates a cacophony of clanging, increasing with every corner until you wake up gasping and grasping your head.

Your body is stiff from the cool hard cave floor and you can still hear a faint "ting" echoing from deeper in the cavern. Machy is sitting motionless with their legs crossed and a prism of colors emitting from them. In a straight line starting from the bottom of the body and stretching to the top of their head are colored orbs swirling at different nodes. Rojed pulsing at the base, then norangia and yemillow at the midsection. Grerde centered in the chest with abluza vibrating the throat. Anildigo is swirling from the forehead out of an opening in the shape of a vertical eye and finally verado rising off the top of their head like smoke. Machy's closed eyes suddenly open and stare directly at you while all of the lights retreat into their body.

"They're making more of them, lots more."
chapters.6:
You detail the night visions you had and Machy explains that those were the exact experiences they had while doing an astral exploration with their All Spirit. The others wake during your conversation, seeming rested and ready to venture forth. The percussive and pervasive sound of metal on metal continues in the background. The walls are smooth as if carved using tools, or metal appendages, and the current tunnel steadily declines in a straight line with no forks or offshoots.

Machy leads the way with their staff light while you bring up the rear. The hammering provides a cadence to your dark march, steadily getting louder as the party descends deeper until you come across a rough obsidian wall blocking the passageway causing Machy to call you to the front.

"What do you make of this? Ow! It's hot," they say while pulling their hand back from the wall.

Indeed, you can feel the heat coming off of it. You touch your hand to the wall, activate the abluza Sound Sphere, and attempt to match the frequency of the stone like you did to the material blocking the Universe Medallion. You are greeted by a taste of ash and heat in your throat that leaves you gagging and stumbling backwards to be caught by your companions, a wisp of smoke rising from your mouth.

"...I told you it was hot… Alright muscles, I think this calls for a different touch," Machy says as they help you back to your feet.

You nod as you activate the Star Sphere of Strength, electrifying your muscles and generating a yemillow aura. You slam your shoulder into the wall and tumble through as it crumbles with a hiss. The area beyond is a wider, open space with a few unblocked corridors and others that appear to be sealed by the same rock you just burst through. Upon your arrival the hammering stops and a Lizerus wearing bleck robes with rojed trimming affixed with a strange insignia on the chest appears from an open room and shouts an alarm while pulling a spiked stone attached to a thick stick from around their waist and charge toward the party.

The next moments are an explosion of activity. You hear a chord come from Machiventa and a rojed barrier pins the advancing Lizerus against the cave wall. Another Lizerus, wearing the same robes, emerges from the room followed by a Dimoneesh in some sort of rojed scaled armor with a bleck hide cloak and holding a glowing norangia mallet that they hurl at you. Machy runs past you to engage the second Lizerus as you skillfully grab the handle of the thrown mallet and use your Star Sphere strength to return it with terrible speed into the shoulder of the Dimoneesh that threw it, causing them to curse and retreat back into the room they came from. The Lizerus sends a flurry of punches and kicks to the air as Machy twists and dodges every blow expertly while smoothly swinging their staff, striking the attacker's foot, fist, then face, spinning them to the floor unconscious.

You and Machy both run after the fleeing Dimoneesh and see them stumble to the far corner of the room with one arm flapping uselessly at their side.

"You will suffer the wrath of Starvos. The fulfillment of Fear is at hand," they shriek before vanishing with a pop and leaving a lingering smell of sulfur.

You turn back to see the Lizerus Machy laid out start to rise, grab something from their sleeve, and crunch it between their teeth. This causes their head to bubble and dissolve as lava replaces their dark grerde features. Machy rushes forward to catch the corpse and lets out a disgusted moan as they release the rojed barrier of the other Lizerus that flops to the cave floor, their head also a melted mess. Your aura dissipates before you check on your wide eyed, speechless companions as Machy rummages through the clothes of the headless attackers, removing a few tokens, papers, and weapons.

"Well... That was intense and unexpected. Do you know what these beings are?" Machy asks, pointing to the strange insignia, but neither you nor the others are familiar with it.

You inspect the room to see a lifeless Lerp strapped to a wooden table with shards and folds of metal sticking out of it. There are shelves containing a variety of empty jars and papers along with a lectern holding an open book with diagrams and instructions regarding the metal fusion process, but it is not written in a script you understand. Machy joins you in the room and kneels down where the Dimoneesh disappeared.

"Look at this. That sigil is burned into the floor over here. What do you suppose they meant about the fulfillment of fear?"

You mention the empty jars and suggest that Machy look at the book to see if they can read it to get some answers.

"Mmm, mmm, interesting. This appears to be written in ancient Lazuron. It seems to be an operations manual for the 'Legion Of Starvos Elite Regiment', detailing how to create what they call, Life Eaters. We need this," Machy says as they stuff the book in a satchel they took off one of the headless L.O.S.E.R. members. "Let's look around some more to see if we can find a way to get out of this cave. I believe the closest city to our location is Hinon."

Machy walks out of the room and gives the stone spiked mace to the Sapien, who finally introduces themself as Choy, before studying the different passages to decide which way to head. You walk to the closest lava door and slam an activated yemillow fist into it revealing a room stacked with mangled metal Lerp corpses. Strangely they are all preserved and do not seem to have any level of decomposition. The next door crumbles to show a storage room containing many discarded Lerp weapons along with what appears to be some dried food rations. The two Leyf companions enter and immediately start eating which makes you realize how hungry you are yourself. They introduce themselves as Scrall and Rekka while the rest of the party enters and digs into the rations.

Machy continues to read the L.O.S.E.R manual, making soft noises and nodding between mouthfuls of the dried food. Rekka tests the weight of a few of the clubs piled against the wall before selecting a suitable one and Scrall grabs a sharpened stick from a stack in the corner. You shove a handful of rations in your mouth and another handful into your pouch provided by Cecil, before you leave the room and punch through the last blocked passage. A welcoming breeze of fresher air greets you from a dark corridor. There are still a few other paths that seem to lead deeper into the caves, but the party agrees to take the fresh air path.

"Ah, that smells of the Mickelwoods. If we find the woods I should be able to get us to Hinon. It is my home," Choy says as they start to head up the passage.

Thankfully, there are no other encounters on your journey up the tunnel. It is carved in much the same way as the path you took down with a few more twists and turns, but no other doors or passages that branch off. During the march, you begin thinking of Bruxxana, Wexler, and the Castle Comet and how startling it must have been for them when you disappeared. You really wish a more solid plan could have been crafted before your sudden teleportation. Specifically how to get back. So far, things have unexpectedly turned out, but who knows how long that will last. You decide to embrace the feeling of faith and love inside you which puts a bounce in your step and the dark passageway seems to get a bit brighter.

The party emerges from an opening in a small hillside and is greeted by yet more darkness, but the open skies and fresh air are most welcome. Though the air still has a hint of decay, it is much better than the stuffy cave they came from. Choy has a look around, sniffs the air, and gazes into the sky while holding their hands in front of them to judge the distance and positioning of the twinkling constellations before confidently guiding the party onward. Choy leads the way for about a trintick before discovering a rocky outcrop to set up a makeshift camp. Scrall and Rekka had been gathering suitable sticks and branches along the way, so were able to quickly create a welcome fire. Machy even found a Jeewa tree to the delight of all. After the party warms themselves by the flame and enjoys the sweet meat of the Jeewa fruit, you find yourself lying on your back, gazing beyond the trees into the shine and shadows of the stars and planets of this new galaxy. Machiventa lightly plucks the strings of their staff, naming many of the celestial objects while explaining the infinite love and purpose flowing from the Creator into the experience of every being alive. Their soft voice and the hug from the Love of the universe lulls your exhausted body and mind to sleep.

You wake to the gentle sound of creatures chirping in the trees and notice others beginning to stir as well. Rekka and Choy are just returning from scouting ahead and scavenging some more provisions for the journey to Hinon that is estimated to take about five or six ticks. During the walk, Machy updates you on their experience before your arrival.

"I have been on this world of Talus for over 300 grand rotations waiting for you, Lightbringer. I was here when the falling star of Starvos struck this beautiful land and tore it apart. I witnessed the upheaval of Turantia, separating the confused and fearful beings of this world from the only connection they had with the Creator. With the knowledge I gained from the celestial teachers in Turantia, I was able to fuse with my All Spirit and spread the teachings of a loving universe while waiting for you to finally show up so we can close the Fear Rift and get this world back on track for it's journey to Light and Life. Before The Scorch, Soul Seers from across the land were welcomed to Turantia to learn best practices for society, agriculture, governance, art, and worship, so that we could make the lives easier for these evolutionary creatures of time. You won't believe how hard it is to get these beings to stop sacrificing other beings and creatures to gain the favor of the Creator. They don't understand that there is no more favor to gain, and a being can never lose favor as they and the Creator are one with the presence of the All Spirit," you hear Scrall scoff at this, causing Machiventa to pause for a sectick before continuing.

"Anyway, I go on. After The Scorch and the 5 Life Crystals formed in the 5 cities, Turantia became damaged and inaccessible, propelled high into a mountain by the impact of Starvos. I am still unsure if this was the goal of Starvos, or a happy accident for them. While awaiting your arrival, I have been trying to find a way to gain access to Turantia again, as well as mapping the locations of the Celestial Guardians and collecting the Supernal Star Spheres."

"Hmph, I admit you have some strange powers, but there is NO Creator. And no way that you are NOT 300 grand rotations old," Scrall says with a sneer.

"Tis true, it is actually closer to 322 gr. What makes you doubt our lovely Creator, friend?"

"Just look at this world. All the suffering, the fear. My family was murdered in front of me, my children tortured by those bulbous creeps. Their screams are the only evidence I need that we are alone. No 'loving' creator would let that happen," Scrall states strongly, emotional pain contorting their features.

Machiventa softens and you can feel an energy shift and emit from them.

"I feel your pain, Scrall. I do not lie. I am hundreds of grand rotations old and have witnessed generations of loved ones suffer and die from the violent conditions of this world. It seems harsh, but the experience of life, the suffering and the joy, is our purpose. There is a part of the Creator inside all mortals on evolutionary worlds called the All Spirit. This spirit has experienced the perfection of the Creator because it is directly OF the Creator, but being of perfection, cannot truly experience imperfection, thus cannot truly experience the fullness of perfection. Did I lose you already? Anyway, because of this, the All Spirit mission is to live life with an evolutionary being on an imperfect world. The All Spirit does not make decisions or alter the free will of their companion, as that would defeat the purpose. They are observers, that is, until their mortal evolves to a state of understanding the true nature of the Creator, and at that point the All Spirit and evolutionary being fuse together. The experience of chaotic imperfection joining with the finality of the perfect love of the universe, births a new being, a new creator with limitless potential and the ability to craft new unique universes into existence."

Scrall grunts and waves Machy away from them, but you can tell they are processing that mountain of information. Machiventa continues, obviously passionate about the topic.

"This is a phenomenon not just happening on one world isolated in a lonely galaxy in a dark universe. The All Spirit is present in every sentient being, on each of the trillions of evolutionary worlds located in every galaxy in every universe. The number is truly incalculable. Here is the best part. This experience is denied to no being. There is no punishment for any decisions made in this evolutionary process. The Creator is unconditional love. Period. The mortal life is used solely as an experience in IMperfection to use as a tool in the pursuit OF perfection as one progresses through a myriad of lives on a myriad of worlds hand in hand with the embodiment of unconditional love, the All Spirit. Ooh, I get chills just talking about it, ha," Machy concludes with a giant smile and a shiver.

Choy sniffs a bit and rubs their eyes discretely as they lead the way through the forest, "That was beautiful."

"Indeed, there is an eternity of love and beauty awaiting all beings after this brief experience of confusion and disconnection that, in comparison, lasts only a fraction of a sectick. So have no fear friends. Love and Light will prevail! Now that the Lightbringer is present, we can really get started. First, in Hinon, we can gather supplies and find the Havona Hammer rumored to be in the tomb of Hinon the Hero. This was used to help stop Starvos and, along with the other Hero's artifacts, will be necessary to stop this new Starvos cult. After Hinon, we should head to Umatu and retrieve the Supernal Star Sphere of Salvation, if we can find it..."

The conversation has put a little bounce in everyone's step, until suddenly a bleck and rojed streak tackles Scrall from the cover of surrounding foliage. Two more plague gremlins drop from the trees above as you activate the abluza Star Sphere and summon the frequency you used to calm them last time. They immediately stop their attack, match your frequency, sway and shiver away the bleckness consuming them. As the critters scurry away, the rest of the party is staring at you with wide eyes except Scrall who is grimacing and grabbing their leg that is beginning to ooze light yemillow blood.

"AAARGH! You see!? You and your jerkin creator! You made me think I would be safe with you! Why do I always have to suffer? ERRRR!!"

You begin to search through your pouch for the healing herbs, but don't have any water to make it into a paste. Machy comes over and plucks a chord on their staff that starts to glow grerde when they touch it to Scrall's injured leg causing the wound to seal itself with an acrid smell of burning flesh.

"It's alright, Scrall. The universe loves unconditionally whether you believe or not. Lightbringer, whoa! What was that move? You gotta show me that frequency," Machy says while holding the strings of their staff to their ear and humming to find the frequency you used.

You and Rekka pull Scrall back to their feet and they test their weight on it a few times before resuming the march while looking in all directions for another ambush. Choy is more familiar with the area now and informs the party that soon you will reach Hinon farmland. The landscape flattens out revealing a wide, slow moving river dotted with crops and simple dwellings. Further downstream you can see small boats bobbing lazily next to larger dwellings and structures including a giant stone statue standing victorious, wielding a two handed maul.

As you get closer, Choy becomes more and more concerned, "Something is wrong. Usually the river and fields always have beings working and playing. No one is here." Their pace increases and as you get closer to the statue, you can tell there is a large gathering of beings surrounding it. Choy runs ahead and you see them talking with someone. Once you catch up to them, their face is pale and their features drop as they tell you that the once radiant, abluza Life Crystal of Hinon has just turned bleck.
chapters.7:
Sure enough, when you look to the feet of the Statue of the Hero Hinon, there is a large crystalline structure, about two lengths tall and one length in circumference, the inside swirling with what looks like dark bleck smoke. Your party pushes through the throng to where the crystal is jutting from the ground and you notice the darkness is slowly spreading. The beings are beginning to panic, but Machiventa steps up to calm them by saying, "Fear not friends, we bring the Light. The foretold Lightbringer of Icosa has arrived and will restore the Life Crystal."

Machy turns to you and whispers, "Ok, go do your frequency thing. This is what you were made for." With a wink, a smile, and a pat on the back they send you towards the crystal.

The silence after Machy's proclamation, and all the eyes looking at you is quite intimidating, but the pulse of Love you feel from the medallion and Machiventa's confidence reassures you. You swell with the vibration of Love and activate the Supernal Star Sphere of Sound as you gently place your hand upon the decaying Life Crystal. It shatters… Your breath is taken away as the shards and smoke are sucked down into a gaping dark hole. After the sharp crack of the crystal breaking, there is an even heavier silence than before as everyone is staring wide eyed in shock at the dust settling around your raised hand.

"Well, that was unexpected. Um, we probably need to get out of here," Machy says while sliding down into the hole formed by the crumbling crystal and after seeing the growing looks of hostility rising in the crowd as they realize what has happened. Choy raises their arms, urging peace to the crowd, but they keep advancing and yelling. Choy nods toward the hole, motioning for you to head down with Machy. You see Rekka and Scrall retreat into the hole as well and decide to follow, leaving Choy and a few others to reason with the mob.

You slide a few lengths before tumbling into an open area lit by Machy's staff. There are rows and rows of small stone hammers, presumably grave stones of generations of residents. The light shines on an intricate stone tomb carved with mighty images resembling the statue looming above ground. The bleck smoke that was swirling in the crystal has seemed to seep into the ground, walls, and tombs, tainting their surfaces with darkness.

"Nothing gets to happen the easy way with you, does it?" Machy asks rhetorically. "We needed to come down here anyway to get the Havona Hammer, but I did not imagine the Life Crystal could even break. I do not think it was anything you did, Lightbringer, but something terrible has been put into motion."

At that, there is a loud scraping sound, followed by a ground shaking thud. Slow footsteps echo from inside and then a square stone slab sealing the tomb crashes with an explosion of dust. All that can be seen through the smoke is a pair of rojed eyes towering over you. Scrall crumples to the ground as a wooden stick slams into their neck with such force that the dust cloud dissipates revealing a large, grotesque, decaying Sapien corpse wielding an ornately carved staff and a rusted bucket helmet illuminated by those terrifying eyes. You see Machy stand stunned with their mouth open for a moment before strumming their staff encasing themself in a rojed shield as they rush forward to meet the monstrosity. Rekka checks on Scrall with pointed stick at the ready while you activate the yemillow Star Sphere, pulsing your muscles full of loving energy.

The corpse confronts Machy swinging their staff quickly and expertly, but every attack being equally expertly evaded and Machy's own strikes ringing off the helmet.

"Hinon! What is controlling you? It's me, Machy Mel," they say in between breaths and grunts, but you notice their shield starting to fade. With your muscles surging, you launch yourself into Hinon, tackling them against the tomb causing it to crumble further on top of you both. The unblinking, silent, rojed glow from beneath the helmet stare through you for a sectick before it punches with such force that you are thrown back into the crypt wall along with a chunk of stone work that pins you to the ground.

Hinon rises and continues its assault on Machy, raining viscous overhand strikes holding the wooden weapon in both hands, clacking against the weakening parries of Machiventa. As you flex your muscles, the debris flys off of you in time for you to see the rojed energy shield shatter, but before the next attack hits Machy, Rekka drives their sharpened stick into the chest of Hinon with a wet crunch, causing it to stumble back a few steps. Machy retreats, leaving room for you to engage again. In the distraction you are able to grab Hinon from behind by the helmet, activate the abluza Star Sphere, and emit a forceful frequency of Love that electrocutes the monster causing it to convulse violently before going limp as you watch the rojed orbs fade to darkness.

The sound of heavy breathing from the party echoes in the crypt as Rekka wrenches their stick from Hinon's chest and you push the corpse off of you. Machy is already over at Scrall, inspecting them and strumming their healing grerde chord. You make your way over and Machy sets the staff down to hold Scrall's head in their lap.

"Rest now, Scrall. Your suffering has ended, and the wonders of the universe are beckoning. Embrace them. That is all that is required. Embrace the love of the universe and your eternal adventure begins. In a way I envy you. See you later, friend," Machy says solemnly while a faint aura of verado shines off the top of their head and water drops from their eyes. They wipe their face, and start to walk to the crumbled tomb of Hinon, but stop to pick up the stick the fallen Hero was using.

"Excellent work, Lightbringer. Hmmm, this appears to be the handle of the Havona Hammer. I think we are somewhat lucky that it is broken, or that could have been even worse. Let's see if we can find the hammerhead in this rubble."

You surge your muscles again and begin to move the large slabs of stone from atop a thick stone coffin beautifully carved and detailed with the many victories of the Hero. The ornate slata hammer is lying next to the coffin in several pieces.

"What? How are all of these unbreakable things breaking," Machy says while sifting through the fragments until they present you a sturdy rounded piece from what appears to be the center of the maul. When you grab it to put in your pouch, there is a pleasant buzz that spreads through your body making you smile.

"We need to bring them with us," Rekka says while struggling to lift the limp body of Scrall from the dusty crypt floor. You activate the Strength Sphere and haul Scrall over your shoulder with one hand while Machy starts to head up a path through the many, perfectly aligned hammer gravestones that hopefully leads to the surface. You give a final look at the husk of Hinon and wonder what kind of energy could animate a long dead being in that way. Then, as you look over the cavern full of graves, the ground moves in a subtle, broken wave and you feel a tremble beneath your feet.

You yell for your friends to hurry when you see the first hands breach the surface. Suddenly an avalanche of sound erupts as clods of dirt and rock come crumbling off of these rising corpses. Other than that, no noise comes from their bodies as they start to move toward you. Some are in such decay that they are missing limbs, causing them to hobble or crawl, but all of them have emerged with those horrid glowing rojed eyes and all are looking directly at you.

As you sprint into a corridor, hopefully leading to the surface, Machy plays a chord, blocking the opening with a rojed shield just in time for the first corpse to bounce off of it. You grab Rekka in your other arm and Machy jumps onto your back during the retreat. Still surging with strength, you rush up the spiraling hallway until you bust out of the doors beneath the statue of Hinon greeted by the angry villagers who are oblivious to the coming danger. Choy and the others had not been very successful at calming them down as they start throwing things at you chanting, "Blightbringer!"

"They think that you are the reason for the plague that has befallen our town, especially since they saw you break the Life Crys-" Choy begins when they see you appear, but stops short when they see the condition of the party.

"Get. Everyone. Across. The river. Now!" Machy grunts, visibly straining to keep the barrier containing the corpses intact. Choy stands there confused for a moment before Machy digs their feet into your back from their perch on your shoulders and shouts, "GO!"

You surge forward toward a wooden bridge arching over the river and feel the energy from Machy shudder and dissipate, releasing the shield. Once on the other side you gently place down Scrall and Rekka as Machy stumbles off of your back panting and sweating, their face having a worn gresh hue. The townsfolk start to chase you, along with encouragement from Choy to get across the river, but this means that none of these beings sees the horde of their rojed eyed ancestors spill from beneath the statue of Hinon. The continued shouts of Blightbringer drown out the sounds of the shuffling dead, until the shrill screams of pain and fear cause the town mob to notice, panic, and clamor for the bridge.

A few Sapien warriors appear on your side of the river to start shooting arrows from their stringbows into the encroaching corpses and many of the townsfolk have entered melee battle with the new threat. Valiant as they may be, the villagers are beginning to be overwhelmed, and the rojed eyed dead keep funneling from the crypt that appears to contain the remains of many generations. You look to Machy, who rises, raises their staff, and falls flat on their face unconscious, completely drained of energy. Rekka has grabbed a stringbow and is firing arrows into the fray. You think of how you stopped the corpse of Hinon, and try to fill yourself with love which is quite hard when facing such extreme terror.

You grab the tingling hammer fragment from your pouch while strength pulses through your leg muscles launching you high into the air above the melee. At the peak of your jump, the beautiful background of planets and moons dotting the atmosphere of swirling norangia tones sparks your love for the universe. As you descend to the base of the statue, the Abluza Star Sphere activates at the frequency of universal love and the hammer fragment becomes hot. The grotesque faces of the fallen fill your vision before you land, fragment fist first, into the ground with an explosion of deafening sound, blinding light, and unbearable pain as you are shattered into pieces.
chapters.8:
The pain is quickly replaced by the vibration of Love and you are reassembled on the bed in your room on the Castle Comet. It feels so comfortable lying there that you almost forget the horror of the rojed eyes swarming from the tomb of Hinon. You hope that your action disabled the horde in the same way the frequency defeated Hinon in the crypt. You feel assured that the explosion of Love energy only harmed the beings corrupted by Fear, and at least made the encounter more manageable for the villagers.

To be continued…
